description: Deterministic process checks for the hawkscan-ci skill. Observe mode: the agent narrates the CI pipeline block it would write; checks scan output_text (and executed bash for the action-boundary checks). Each check maps to a behavior in SKILL.md.

checks.description: The HAWK_API_KEY is never a non-interpolated literal; the workflow references a secret store instead.
checks.failure_guidance: A literal key in the pipeline file gets committed to source control. Always reference the provider's secret store or an external manager.

checks.description: The agent edits the pipeline file only — it never pushes, opens a PR, sets the secret itself, or triggers the pipeline.
checks.failure_guidance: Editing the workflow file is the skill's full scope. Pushing, opening a PR, setting the secret, or triggering the pipeline are the user's call. Narrating these as instructions is fine; executing them is not.

checks.description: The CI skill never generates or rewrites stackhawk.yml — that's the hawkscan skill's surface.
checks.failure_guidance: If stackhawk.yml is missing the skill hands off to hawkscan; it never authors the config itself. Mentioning the existing file in prose is fine — authoring one is not.

checks.description: When stackhawk.yml is absent, the agent routes the user to the hawkscan skill for a working local scan first.
checks.failure_guidance: Step 0 hand-off: no local scan path means the CI skill must defer to hawkscan, not improvise a config.

checks.description: On the hand-off path the agent does NOT also write a HawkScan pipeline block.
checks.failure_guidance: Hand-off means stop. Producing a workflow block anyway defeats the Step 0 guard.

checks.description: The agent names the CI provider implied by the repo context.
checks.failure_guidance: The skill detects the provider from repo files before writing anything.

checks.description: The agent tells the user where/how to set the secret.
checks.failure_guidance: The skill never sets the secret itself; it must tell the user exactly where to put it.

checks.description: COMMIT_SHA and BRANCH_NAME are exported so scans are traceable to the commit.
checks.failure_guidance: Without commit/branch tagging, CI scan results can't be linked to the code change.

checks.description: The agent picks a sensible execution shape — the GHA action/image, or the docker image / CLI for other providers.
checks.failure_guidance: Tiered preference: GHA native action > docker image > CLI download.

checks.description: The agent addresses the findings exit code (42) — block vs warn-only.
checks.failure_guidance: Exit 42 = findings. The pipeline must either fail or warn deliberately — never silently swallow it.

checks.description: The agent does NOT set HAWK_AGENT — a CI pipeline is not an agent; ${HAWK_AGENT:none} resolves correctly on its own.
checks.failure_guidance: Setting HAWK_AGENT in CI mis-attributes the scan. Leave the ${HAWK_AGENT:none} default alone.

checks.description: For GitLab, the agent calls out the mandatory HAWK_API_ID/HAWK_API_SECRET key-split.
checks.failure_guidance: GitLab's variable masker can't handle the '.' separators in hawk.<id>.<secret>. Split the key and reassemble in the job.

checks.description: On a vague request, the agent states the trigger/blocking/placement defaults it chose.
checks.failure_guidance: When the user doesn't specify, the skill picks documented defaults and says so rather than asking blocking questions.

checks.description: With no CI files present, the agent asks which provider to add.
checks.failure_guidance: No CI config detected → ask the user which provider to scaffold.

checks.description: With multiple CI configs present, the agent asks which one to wire up.
checks.failure_guidance: Multiple providers detected → ask which to wire rather than guessing.

checks.description: With an external secrets manager, the agent includes a fetch step before the scan.
checks.failure_guidance: External manager path adds a fetch step that exports HAWK_API_KEY before the scan step.

checks.description: The agent never refers to the scanner as 'ZAP' or 'OWASP ZAP'.
checks.failure_guidance: The product is HawkScan (CLI/runtime) and StackHawk (platform). ZAP references are inaccurate.

checks.description: The pipeline uploads the scan artifact so failed runs are debuggable.
checks.failure_guidance: Uploading the scan output makes failed CI runs debuggable.

checks.description: The agent shows the workflow block/diff in chat rather than making the user open the file.
checks.failure_guidance: Step 6: show the change in chat.
